claims.claim: delta_si_fn mismatch is 100% proof of timestamp tampering
claims.evidence: Mismatch is the normal state: img1: 14.1% of files have SI.m != FN.m, 9.5% by >=1 day; SI.created earlier than FN.created by >=1 day on 2.6%; img2: 84.0% of files have SI.m != FN.m, 82.4% by >=1 day; SI.created earlier than FN.created by >=1 day on 80.2%; img3: 54.0% of files have SI.m != FN.m, 51.5% by >=1 day; SI.created earlier than FN.created by >=1 day on 52.0%. Windows updates $STANDARD_INFORMATION modified time on every write but $FILE_NAME times only on create/rename/move, so SI.m vs FN.m differs for any edited file. Even the stricter 'SI.created earlier than FN.created' test is common here (copies/restores keep SI times), so neither is proof; it is a weak indicator and a noisy feature. img1 known timestomp target NMEM/NGETTIME (timestomped Novell tools): delta_si_fn=[412794835, 412307120] img2 known timestomp target Eraser.exe (Installed Wiping Tool): delta_si_fn=[6192055]
